references.text: Abraham rose early in the morning (וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר) – the same phrasing as in 22:3, showing Abraham's pattern of immediate obedience to God's word.
The book of Hebrews highlights Abraham's faith when he was tested and was willing to offer Isaac, believing that God could raise him from the dead.
James uses Abraham's offering of Isaac as an example that faith was completed by works, directly linked to his actions in Genesis 22.
Paul discusses Abraham's faith and justification, which is the background for his obedient actions described in Genesis 22.

Continuation of the journey: Isaac carries the wood, Abraham carries the fire and the knife, and they arrive at the place where he builds the altar and binds Isaac – the completion of the preparations in verse 3.
'I hastened and did not delay to keep your commands' – an expression of the same immediate obedience that Abraham showed when he rose early to do what God said.
Direct narrative continuation of the readiness for sacrifice at the same place.
New Testament theological interpretation revealing the nature of faith in Abraham's offering.
Places the offering in the context of God's promise to give Isaac as an heir.
